chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Rifa'ah ibn Musa, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who arrives in the month of Ramadan from travel until he sees that he will enter his home in the forenoon or mid-morning. He said: 'When the dawn breaks and he is outside (not yet entered), he has the choice: if he wishes, he fasts, and if he wishes, he breaks his fast.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a traveler arriving home after Fajr in Ramadan?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the status of a traveler who crosses the threshold of their hometown after Fajr has already broken, granting them the discretion (*al-khiyar*) to either complete the day's fast or break it. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view that the obligation to fast is contingent upon being a resident (*muqim*) at the time of Fajr, distinguishing it from the Hanafi position which often requires fasting once the fast is begun. The hadith underscores the flexibility granted to travelers in Shia fiqh, prioritizing ease (*taysir*) while maintaining the sanctity of the month.
